prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1099; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following report of a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was stopped at the light when struck from behind by a third-party vehicle. Claimant reports neck pain and stiffness, and has not yet sought medical treatment. Photos of both vehicles requested from the insured.

Entry 2: Spoke with the claimant by phone. Claimant reports onset of neck pain and headache within hours of the collision and says a family physician visit is planned. Claimant is not represented by an attorney and has asked for guidance on the claims process. Explained the steps for submitting medical records and vehicle repair estimates.

Entry 3: Received the police report from the responding agency. It lists the rear vehicle driver as cited for following too closely. Witness statement from a passenger in the stopped vehicle is consistent with the claimant's account. Liability appears clear at this stage.

Entry 4: Claimant returned a signed medical authorization form and a preliminary note from the treating clinic diagnosing whiplash-associated disorder with a recommendation for physical therapy. Reviewed the clinic record for consistency with the reported mechanism of injury. No prior neck complaints noted in the records provided.

Entry 5: Vehicle inspection completed by the independent appraiser. Rear bumper, trunk lid, and taillight assembly damage confirmed. Repair estimate received and under review. Claimant informed that the injury portion of the claim remains open pending completion of physical therapy and a final medical report.
